Jessica / Priyom / Laura — putting the remediation status in one place below. I referenced and linked the internal tickets where the work is tracked. Evidence artifacts will be attached to the packet and a copy uploaded to the Drive link in the manifest.

1) Auth (finding A-21) — STATUS: Closed (prod)
- Summary: JWT expiration default was set to 90 days due to a config parsing bug in the session service. Patch deployed 2026-11-05 and configuration hard-coded to 24h max.
- Evidence: token config export (auth-service:/config/jwt.json), deployment diff, unit test showing expiry enforcement.
- ETA: N/A (already in prod, rolled to all regions).
- Ticket: JIRA-SEC-348

2) Logging (finding L-07) — STATUS: In progress (canary)
- Summary: Added session start/end events and enriched context (user_id, request_id, route). Implementation completed in canary on 2026-11-12; rolling to 30% production traffic for 72 hours.
- Evidence: canary logs samplings (redacted PII), logging config (rsyslog/nginx filter rules), instrumentation PR and code snippets.
- ETA to full prod: 2026-11-24 (pending canary validation).
- Ticket: JIRA-SEC-349

3) Secrets (finding S-05) — STATUS: Closed (remediated)
- Summary: Found plaintext API keys in a legacy backup snapshot in S3; removed snapshot, rotated affected keys, and added lifecycle policy + object-level encryption enforcement.
- Evidence: S3 object inventory CSV (redacted), rotation audit entries, KMS key rotation log.
- ETA: N/A (remediated 2026-11-08).
- Ticket: JIRA-SEC-350

4) Network (finding N-12) — STATUS: In progress (under review)
- Summary: Management ports were reachable from a public subnet due to a misconfigured route table on a staging VPC. We've updated the route and applied Security Group restrictions; running a validation scan across affected subnets.
- Evidence: route table before/after snapshots, security group rule exports, validation scan results pending.
- ETA to closure: 2026-11-22 (pending final scan verification).
- Ticket: JIRA-SEC-351

5) Permissions (finding P-03) — STATUS: In progress (partial)
- Summary: Several service accounts had overly broad roles. We've applied least-privilege role bindings to core services and created a remediation playbook for the remaining service accounts.
- Evidence: IAM bindings diff, remediation playbook, service account audit.
- ETA to full remediation: 2026-11-30 (we will provide incremental evidence by 24 Nov).
- Ticket: JIRA-SEC-352

Attachments for the packet: redwood_pen_test_summary_redacted.pdf (redacted report), pt_evidence_manifest_q4_2026.xlsx (mapping table that points to which artifact corresponds to which finding), and per-ticket evidence bundles.

Notes:
- We've redacted PII from logs and inventories.
- We will provide a SOC 2 control mapping matrix one-off if you need the pen test findings mapped to specific Trust Services Criteria.

Please let us know if you need pcaps or raw object listings (we prefer redacted exports for data minimization).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
